clue.text: Bear in pre-hibernation initially putting on weight

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word pre-hibernation

parts.note: putting on, as in putting on weight, means adding
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A bear fattening up just before it settles down for the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru found at a London railway station.

clue.text: A little chihuahua dog appears around temple

indicators.note: around means the hidden letters are turned the other way
A little says only a small part of the following words is used, hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A tiny dog shows up near a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the definition but is part of the hidden stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple.

clue.text: Formal letter, nineteenth one penned by physician today ultimately

indicators.note: penned by means the letter is enclosed by the other pieces

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of today

parts.note: S is the nineteenth letter of the alphabet, spelt out as ess

explanation.surface: A doctor writes a formal letter today.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothing is smart and elegant, suitable for formal occasions.

clue.text: Idea minister rued occasionally to reform brokers

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the collected letters are rearranged
occasionally means only every other letter of rued is used

explanation.surface: A minister regrets an idea to overhaul the brokers.
explanation.definitionFit: Brokers act as go-betweens arranging deals, which is what intermediaries do.

clue.text: Fuel leakage when key parts crack

indicators.note: parts, as a verb, means the crack opens up to admit the other pieces

parts.note: to gape is to crack or split open
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A gas leak happens when the key components split.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas escape is a leak of gas, a fuel used for heating and cooking.

clue.text: Admitted having had debts, concealing indefinite number

indicators.note: concealing means the first word hides the number inside it

parts.note: owed means having had debts
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to debts while hiding how many there were.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own, is to confess, so owned means admitted.

clue.text: Reduce high speed

definitions.meaning: a ... is a fast pace, as in 'going at a ...'

explanation.surface: An instruction to slow down from a fast pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping trims something shorter, and a brisk pace is called a good clip.

clue.text: Detective, hard on upset mum in London borough

parts.note: Lewis is a TV detective, from Inspector Morse and its spin-off
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: ma is another word for mum

explanation.surface: A detective is tough on a distressed mother in a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewisham is a borough in south-east London.

clue.text: To some extent rising cadet is a rapacious sponger

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming cadet is somewhat of a greedy freeloader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads upwards, so backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others without giving back, just as a sponger does.

clue.text: Musical instrument underneath stairs in black box

indicators.note: underneath in a down clue puts this piece below the next one

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
the recorder is a simple woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: An instrument stored in the cupboard under the stairs, inside a black box.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's black box is the flight recorder that logs data for crash investigators.

clue.text: Visitor is supposed to be announced

indicators.note: to be announced means the word must be spoken out loud, so we want what it sounds like

parts.note: to be supposed is to be guessed

explanation.surface: A caller who is expected to be introduced on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is supposed' looks like it belongs to 'Visitor', but it gives GUESSED, which sounds like GUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone visiting a home or event at another's invitation.

clue.text: Newspaper fine with subordinate making enormous bloomer

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
lower means of junior rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: A tabloid and a junior employee together produce a huge blunder in print.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' is a British word for a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms; THE SUN is a UK tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunflowers are famously tall plants with very large flower heads, so a giant bloomer.

clue.text: Wants daughter to meet English gentlemen possessing energy!

indicators.note: possessing means the first word holds the next one inside it

parts.note: sirs is a form of address for gentlemen
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A wish for a daughter to be introduced to some lively English gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires as a verb means longs for or wants, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Grasps biscuits I've put out

indicators.note: put out means the letters of I've are thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: digestives are a common British plain biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone throwing out biscuits they had grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGESTIVES are plain wholemeal British biscuits, often dunked in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to take it in and understand it, as grasping does.

clue.text: Stubborn Republican about to block review of Tennessee report

indicators.note: to block means the word for about is lodged inside the reversed letters
review, read as re-view or looking back, says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee
an article is a report in a newspaper
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A US politician obstructs an inquiry into a report from Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' is read as looking back, turning the pair round to give ELCITRANT; 'to block' then lodges the circa abbreviation just after its opening E.
explanation.definitionFit: A recalcitrant person obstinately refuses to obey or cooperate, which is being stubborn.

clue.text: Note Yorkshire's opener becoming short-tempered

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: opener means just the first letter of Yorkshire, as an opening batsman goes first

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire cricket opener getting tetchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests an opening batsman in cricket; Yorkshire is an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety means grumpy and irritable, easily angered.

clue.text: Type of spaniel in season, mother-to-be essentially

parts.note: spring is a season

indicators.note: essentially means the essence or central letters of mother-to-be

explanation.surface: A spaniel in season becomes a mother-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a breed of gundog used to flush game.

clue.text: Queue endlessly to get disinfectant

indicators.note: endlessly means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: to queue is to form a line

explanation.surface: Waiting in a queue for some disinfectant.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin is a formaldehyde solution used as a disinfectant and preservative.

clue.text: Expert against healthy characters eating European pastries

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional

indicators.note: eating means the following pieces take the letter for European inside them

parts.note: fit means healthy
roles are characters played by actors

explanation.surface: A specialist argues against healthy people tucking into European pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' only places PRO beside what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are small choux pastry buns filled with cream, often covered in chocolate.

clue.text: Harsh neighbourhood police officer must flee

indicators.note: must flee means the officer leaves the area, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a district is a neighbourhood or area
DI is Detective Inspector, a police rank

explanation.surface: A tough local constable has to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means severe and demanding, close to harsh.

clue.text: Forked out around two pounds for pasty

indicators.note: around means the payment word wraps round the pounds

parts.note: to fork out is to pay, so forked out is paid
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two are LL

explanation.surface: Paying a couple of pounds for a pasty, a Cornish meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie but means pale-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid and pasty both describe a pale, unhealthy complexion.

clue.text: Unscrupulous male this writer's spoken about

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces go round the letter for male

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I; this writer's is I'm, I am
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: The setter remarks that he has spoken of a dishonest man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immoral lacks moral principles, so is unscrupulous.

clue.text: Subject, say, covered by story

indicators.note: covered by means the example abbreviation is enclosed by the word for story

parts.note: a story can mean a lie
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A topic, for instance, tucked inside a narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' reads as a topic but is a person owing allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege can be a vassal bound to serve a lord, that is, a subject.

clue.text: Terrible actor content to leave India for another country

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word actor is badly mangled into a new order
content to leave means the inside letters of India go, keeping just its ends

explanation.surface: A poor actor happy to quit India for a new country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as 'happy' but is the inner letters of India; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country on the Adriatic, another nation besides India.

clue.text: Duck out of Bond film

explanation.surface: A duck emerging from a James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves both a species of diving duck and a 007 movie.

clue.text: Primate dismissing bishop perhaps as bore

indicators.note: dismissing means the chess piece is sent away from the primate

parts.note: a mandrill is a large primate, a kind of baboon
a bishop is an example of a chess man

explanation.surface: A senior churchman being sacked as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' and 'bishop' suggest the church, but the primate is the animal and the bishop a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bores holes, so drill and bore are synonyms as verbs or nouns.

clue.text: Spoke of career before golf

indicators.note: before places the run ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a career as a verb means to run
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sporting figure talks about their career before taking up golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past of speak; it is the noun, a rung or crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is a ladder's crossbar, and spoke is an old word for such a rung.

clue.text: Dry hay tedder spreads across field at last

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch round the extra letter
spreads suggests the letters of hay tedder are scattered into a new order
at last tells us to use the final letter of field

explanation.surface: A haymaking machine spreading hay across a field to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: A tedder is a farm machine that spreads hay; 'spreads' rearranges HAYTEDDER round the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehydrated means having had its water removed, which is dried.
